page: Google Cloud Platform f1-micro is a shared-core instance within the f1 server family. It features 1 vCPU mapped to a shared physical Intel Xeon core with 1 thread and an x86_64 architecture. The instance is equipped with 0.6 GB of system memory, which equates to 0.6 GB per core. It does not include any local NVMe storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the f1-micro operates in the bottom 10% of performance across all tested categories. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests both recorded a score of 384.79. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 80.8 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 0.2 GB/sec. Passmark CPU and memory scores are low, with the overall CPU score at 236.08 and the database operations score registering at 0.0.

Due to its shared CPU allocation and minimal memory capacity, this instance is designed for low-intensity workloads. It achieves a static web serving throughput of 0.22 GB/sec and handles 0.24 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. The primary tradeoff is the highly restricted resource profile, making it unsuitable for database hosting, heavy computation, or memory-intensive tasks. It is best utilized for basic utility scripts, lightweight cron jobs, or simple development and testing environments where cost minimization is prioritized over performance.
